A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAG framework, with matching architecture, equations, and experiments. Their text, figures, tables, and appendices A–B are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting results, component ablations, and sensitivity experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original forecasting and ablation results and reports expanded evaluations without future covariates and new prediction visualizations.

M1.justification: The embeddings, query/key parameter transfer, gated attention fusion, prediction fusion, and combined L1 losses remain unchanged. Both versions also substitute predicted future covariates when actual future covariates are unavailable. Renaming the causal modules as correlation modules does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: The eight-dataset standard benchmark result suite in v1 Tables 1 and 6 disappears, although its dataset descriptions remain and Electricity survives in model analyses. Evaluation without future covariates expands from five real-world datasets to all twelve, adding BE, FR, Rapel, and the four Sdwpf subsets under this input condition.

E2.justification: xPatch is removed from the reported future-covariate comparisons, despite remaining in the baseline description. The historical-only comparison expands from four to nine baselines, adding TFT, TiDE, Amplifier, TimeKAN, and DLinear alongside TimeXer, CrossLinear, DUET, and PatchTST.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation drops the common-benchmark schedule using a lookback of 96 and horizons 96, 192, 336, and 720. The retained real-world lookback/horizon pairs, data splits, metrics, training settings, and historical-only inference procedure remain unchanged. The new main-text implementation subsection largely repeats v1 Appendix A.2.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix B.4 and Figures 6–7 add NP prediction case studies comparing forecasts with and without future covariates. The component ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, and lookback-window analyses are retained; v1 Figures 4–5 correspond to v2 Figures 5–4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests for the original forecasting experiments.

E6.justification: The historical-only results are expanded and several DAG scores change. Under the same reported settings, Colbun at horizon 30 changes from MSE/MAE 0.180/0.223 to 0.161/0.208, while NP at horizon 24 changes from 0.226/0.255 to 0.237/0.259. Standard-benchmark and xPatch result entries are removed. All shared prediction-error values in v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The time-series definitions, forecasting formulation, attention equations, and loss formulations are mathematically unchanged. Equation renumbering and notation adjustments introduce no new assumptions, derivations, proofs, or mathematical corrections.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion redefine the central contribution from discovering and injecting causal relationships to discovering and injecting correlations. This changes the claimed nature of what DAG learns. The overarching forecasting advantage and public dataset/code contributions remain claimed in the introduction.

C2.justification: Sections 4–5 reinterpret the transferred attention parameters and ablation benefits as correlation modeling rather than causal discovery. New Appendix B.4 also attributes the NP prediction examples to successful dual correlation modeling. The reframing is incomplete: Section 1 retains assertions about causal dependencies and dual causality, and no substantive limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: v2 removes the explicit variant-by-variant ablation descriptions, including their auxiliary-loss usage, and the standard-benchmark horizon instructions. Most reproducibility information remains identical: dataset statistics, Python/PyTorch setup, A800 hardware, optimizer and batch-size policy, MLP-fusion pseudocode, and code/data access disclosure.

R1.justification: DAG's claimed distinction from TiDE/TFT shifts from causal constraints to fuller correlation modeling. v2 adds GCGNet and contrasts its graph modeling with DAG's separation of variable roles and time periods. It also substantially prunes background references, including CALF, TimeBridge, and the original N-BEATS and DeepAR entries, while retaining much of the core exogenous-forecasting survey.

P1.justification: Most exposition and the top-level section sequence remain recognizable. v2 condenses the abstract and conclusion, changes terminology and the author list, reorders model analyses, moves sensitivity discussion into the appendix, and promotes existing implementation information into the main text. A generic Impact Statement is added.

P2.justification: The document switches from ACM styling to a different preprint layout and extensively reorganizes its displays. Main results become compact horizon averages with full results in the appendix; standard-benchmark tables disappear, the historical-only table expands, sensitivity plots move, and two NP visualization grids are added. Architecture figures are relabeled without changing their structure.

improvement.justification: The correlation framing better matches the unchanged attention-based method, and the expanded historical-only comparisons strengthen evidence for its practical fallback. However, v2 removes xPatch and broader benchmark results while continuing to list that baseline and describe those experiments; its introduction also retains causal assertions. Improved claim calibration and practical evaluation therefore coexist with reduced comparative evidence and new reporting mismatches, leaving the net quality direction unclear.
